title: Asymptotic Entanglement Hiding under Stabilizer Restrictions
authors: Jicun Li, Wei Xie, Jun Wu, Honglin Chen, Xiang-Yang Li
abstract: Entanglement is central to quantum information processing, while stabilizer operations underpin fault-tolerant quantum computation. We ask how much entanglement remains visible or distillable under stabilizer restrictions. We quantify stabilizer-visible entanglement by restricting the measured relative entropy of entanglement to stabilizer measurements, thereby obtaining converse bounds on entanglement distillation under stabilizer operations. We demonstrate magic-free asymptotic entanglement hiding: we construct explicit convex mixtures of pure stabilizer states on $N$ qutrits per party whose unrestricted visible entanglement and LOCC-distillable entanglement both grow as $Ω(N/\log N)$, while their stabilizer-visible and stabilizer-distillable entanglement vanish as $N\to\infty$. Thus, an unbounded amount of LOCC-distillable entanglement carried by stabilizer states can become asymptotically invisible and undistillable under stabilizer restrictions. We further prove that stabilizer-visible entanglement is $O(1)$ with high probability for Haar-random pure states despite extensive unrestricted visibility, and vanishes uniformly over entangled Werner states as the local dimension grows through odd primes. These results reveal a fundamental separation between entanglement and magic as resources, exposing intrinsic limits on entanglement extraction using stabilizer operations.
summary: This paper establishes a fundamental separation between entanglement and 'magic' by quantifying how much entanglement remains visible when measurements are restricted to stabilizer operations. Through explicit constructions, the authors show that entanglement can be asymptotically hidden, meaning the distillable entanglement can be large while the stabilizer-visible entanglement vanishes. This reveals intrinsic limitations on entanglement extraction using only stabilizer operations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental operational difference between entanglement visible under general measurements (LOCC) versus entanglement visible only through stabilizer measurements.
main_result: They demonstrate 'magic-free asymptotic entanglement hiding,' showing that highly entangled states can possess arbitrarily large LOCC-distillable entanglement while having vanishing entanglement visible under stabilizer restrictions.
method: The analysis involves constructing explicit convex mixtures of stabilizer states and applying bounds derived from the relative entropy and Wigner function analysis to quantify the gap between different entanglement measures.
model_or_system: The study uses bipartite quantum states, specifically focusing on $N$ qutrits per party, Haar-random pure states, and Werner states, all analyzed within the framework of stabilizer operations.
key_observables: Stabilizer-visible entanglement ($	ext{ESTAB}$), Unrestricted visible entanglement ($	ext{EALL}$), and LOCC-distillable entanglement ($ED_{LOCC}$).
important_parameters: The number of qutrits per party ($N$), the local dimension ($p$, an odd prime), and the state parameter ($t$ for Werner states).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is the restriction of measurements to the set of stabilizer operations, which defines the 'magic' resource theory.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the entanglement hiding mechanism by comparing the unrestricted visible entanglement (solid curve) to the stabilizer-restricted bound (dashed curve) for an interpolated state.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining the measures, then proving the gap for specific states (Werner states, mixed stabilizer states), and finally establishing the asymptotic scaling laws for general mixed stabilizer states.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, quantitative measure of how much quantum correlation is 'hidden' from computation protocols relying only on stabilizer measurements, which is crucial for understanding the limits of fault-tolerant quantum computation.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Mixed-stabilizer visibility gap. For ρ(s) = (1 −s)σ∗+ sρ∗, the solid curve gives the exact unre- stricted value EALL(ρ(s)) = D(ρ(s)∥σ∗). The dashed curve is DKL(Wρ(s)∥Wσ∗), the Wigner–KL upper bound on ESTAB(ρ(s)). Since this certified upper bound is strictly smaller than EALL(ρ(s)) for every s > 0, stabilizer measure- ments are strictly weaker than unrestricted measurements for this mixed-stabilizer family.
